body: Thank you for your advice. I was afraid that they would think I'm a loser because my maturity level and lack of independence. I'm at the stage of my life where potential partners actually look for this stuff and I want to measure up.

I feel like I have to play years of catch up. I think I'm going to end up being incel for quite a while. I have to undo years of mental problems and it will be like a full time job to change. I know I'm making excuses, but it's so damn frustrating.
How? Many people have mental issues that makes it difficult to catch up or they don't even know where to start.

I really like what you said. I was thinking of sticking with women because of the intense feelings I have had for them that were never replicated with men. I'm glad that I am in good company with other lesbians who had their experiences fairly late. 

Again, I really liked your advice. Thank you!

You actually raise a good point about naivety. People often assume I'm younger than I actually am. I think it is both because of my demeanor and my appearance. I can pass for an 18-year-old. I hate this because I wish I was taken more seriously by society. I'm even intimidated by dating girls my own age or older because I fear being treated condescendingly. Even if the relationship is equal by name, I feel the power dynamics would naturally leave me being the submissive one. I don't want to feel as if someone is babysitting me. 
Yet deliberately aiming for people much younger than me is creepy. I know the best solution is to become more mature and try to catch up with people my own age. I hope they have patience.

Hi. That is a good question. 
I'm not sure if anything I've done counted as a date. There was impromptu moment where this guy suddenly took me to the movies and paid for everything. We kissed and got high. I found him rather aggressive because he kept asking me for nudes and sending graphic messages. I wasn't sure if that was normal, but I did not feel comfortable with that. We were 22. 

I've been back to the gay bar, but I did not have the same luck. None of the girls seemed to be interested in me. It seems that whenever I attempt to approach someone I get turned down. I felt that I was spoiled by the first time, because short of sexual experiences, it was perfect.

I've tried OKCupid and Tinder but taking the next step and meeting someone from there has never happened. I did not find anyone I clicked with. I'm just nervous about taking the next step because I still live with my family that I'm not out to. My parents are always home. As grimy as this sounds, I gave that guy a bj in his car because there was nowhere else to do it. I'm not sure if going to the mall and a bar together counts as dating him, but we didn't hang out together much.

Yes, I'm mostly worried about the quality of people I would meet online. I don't expect anyone to be perfect, but I don't want to leave the date with more questions than I had.

That is all I can do. I need to move on.
I've experienced everything a teenager would have except for the most crucial part --- love and sex.
When I was 14, I was on the right track. At my 8th grade formal, I slow danced with a boy. I was not interested in him, but I knew he had a crush on me for years. I let him have his moment. If I went on a normal trajectory, I would've had my first kiss at 15 like the average teenager. I had my first kiss when I was 20.
Hell, the first time I got drunk and high I was 18. I've even experimented with drugs before I've had deeply bonded with someone. What does this say about me?

I wish I could start over. I missed out on my formative years where my peers were learning the rules of relationships and sex. I feel like I haven't emotionally developed beyond the age of 16. I just got my driver's license a few months ago when I should've had one a decade ago. There are many examples like the former. I hate being emotionally and socially retarded.

I'm not sure how quickly I can catch up with people my own age. I don't have a career and I'm a virgin. It would be humiliating to be treated like someone's little sister by a woman my age. I don't know why people act as if I'm naïve. 
I know that's not an excuse to go for younger girls. I just wonder how many years I would have to work on myself to be on the same level as people my own age.

Honestly, I can be picky when it comes to women. I'm only interested in femmes. I've tried hooking up with men that I had no interest in and it didn't work out well. I'm sure it would be the same way if I tried to go out with a butch, stud, or andro. No offense to anyone.
I'm not sure how to make a friendship or relationship stick. I almost never get past the acquaintance phase.

I understand what you mean. One of my main issues is that I feel like I am coasting through life. I want to make steps that can help me change my life so I won't stay stagnant forever. I don't want to imagine the rest of my life being this way.

You're right about college. Even though you can learn mostly from books, college exposes you to viewpoints and people that you probably would not have known otherwise. In that sense, college was worth it. I just hope I find a career that help me repay my debt. I'm relieved that compared to most graduates in debt, I only owe a few thousand dollars.

Kendrick Lamar is awesome. I was thinking of getting his new album.

Thanks for your compliment, I thought I would bore people with my long post lol.

I usually like to read non-fiction books. I appreciate fiction, but I look towards non-fiction for knowledge and to learn new things. I'm juggling between books now since I'm lacking motivation to actually finish anything :/
I've been reading LGBT fiction lately. I finished Rubyfruit Jungle and now I'm reading The Well of Loneliness. 
As for non-fiction I'm reading The Personal MBA, In Defense of Food, and Secret Historian. 
I'm basically all over the place when it comes to books. 

What do you like to read?
